name: manual_230c6d
claim: GitHub access discovery, the most consequential finding of this week: the oramasys org's GitHub REST API (api.github.com/*) returns 403 on EVERY endpoint -- including fully unauthenticated, zero-token requests -- for repos that are genuinely public (confirmed: github.com/oramasys, github.com/oramasys/perpetua-core both return 200 and are readable). This is a real org-level API-access policy, not a token-scope limitation, and it blocked over a week of direct verification of oramasys/perpetua-core PR #1 despite the repo being open-source. The actual workaround, found only this week: plain web_fetch against ordinary github.com web pages (org profile, /pulls list, individual /pull/N conversation pages) is NOT blocked by this policy at all -- it returns full page content including PR descriptions, commit lists, and inline CodeRabbit review comments. This was a genuine gap in approach across many prior sessions/turns, not a true access wall: the API was tried exclusively and repeatedly declared "still blocked" without ever testing whether a different tool (plain HTTP page fetch vs. REST API) could see around the same org policy. Confirmed directly via this method: oramasys/perpetua-core PR #1 ("refactor(graph): final MiniGraph reconciliation", diazMelgarejo, opened Aug 26 2026) is real, open, mergeable, currently at head commit 876a4581f1016735ec3bf1c1475cd11cc76a5bab (12 commits), with baseline main@8c063f4 recording 62 passing tests before this PR's changes. As of two independent checks this week (both returning identical head SHA, confirming no drift), two CodeRabbit review findings remain genuinely open and unfixed on that real PR: (1) PerpetuaState.merge()'s more precise delta-aliasing bug -- model_copy(deep=True) deep-copies the EXISTING model but applies update=delta afterward without deep-copying delta's own values, so a caller-held mutable reference passed in delta still aliases across state generations; orama-system's own docs (01-kernel-spec.md) were corrected to the complete fix (model_copy(update=copy.deepcopy(delta), deep=True), verified against all three isolation properties directly) but this correction has not yet been ported back into the real perpetua-core code as of this check; (2) .github/workflows/test.yml's actions/checkout@v4 step does not set persist-credentials: false, flagged CWE-522 by zizmor SAST -- pull-request-controlled test code can access the persisted contents token, unfixed as of this check.

decisions.notes: Direct instruction to record the week, especially GitHub access -- this is the single most consequential, previously-unrecorded finding: a real access-method discovery plus two freshly-reconfirmed still-open findings on the actual perpetua-core PR.
